role: fresh independent anti-anchored source/publication review of GDValue after canonical public descent extraction
additional_inputs: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.07006v1#S3: Lemma3.1, Theorem3.4 (3.1)-(3.3), Lemma3.5 and following weighted proof
whole_module_review: Read the complete current GDValue module with both public proofs. The old private descent theorem is absent; the import and both descent calls use GradientDescentBasic.gradient_step_descent_of_quadratic_upper_bound. Read the full current shared Basic source and verified its h>=0, beta h<=1 and upper-model premises match those at both call sites. Both lessons replace the private-helper explanation with the exact canonical public name and list it in ASTIS dependencies. This review does not rely on an immutable historical acceptance.

mathematical_review.shared_descent: For g=gradient f(x), s=x-hg, upper model gives f(s)-f(x)<=(-h+beta h^2/2)||g||^2. Multiplying beta h<=1 by h||g||^2>=0 yields the -h/2 estimate. No beta sign or differentiability is needed for this model-based algebra. GDValue callers independently assume C1, so gradient is their genuine Frechet derivative representative.
mathematical_review.energy: First-order support gives f(z)>=f(x)-<g,x-z>+alpha||x-z||^2/2. Multiplying by 2h>=0, inserting descent and expanding ||x-z-hg||^2 cancels the h^2||g||^2 term. Alpha,beta need not be nonnegative and z need not minimize f.
mathematical_review.weighted: With Xn=T^[n]x0 and q=1-alpha h>=0, establish u_(n+1)<=q u_n-2h gap_(n+1), and descent gives antitone gaps. Product-form Gronwall accepts signed forcing. Because -2h<=0 and q^k>=0, earlier gaps may be replaced by the final gap in the upper bound; discard u_N>=0 and reflect the finite index to obtain exactly 2h sum(q^k)gap_N<=q^N u0.
mathematical_review.endpoints: No inverse is used: N=0 gives zero sum and 0<=u0; h=0 gives identity T and zero left coefficient; q=0 keeps q^0=1 and the last forcing term; q=1 gives sum=N; q>1 is permitted under signed negative alpha. No strict decay or normalization is implied in those cases.
mathematical_review.source_boundaries: Euclidean C2 and nonnegative source moduli specialize the current C1 Hilbert statements. h>=0 is necessary in the proof and omitted from the printed restriction. Source (3.3) permits arbitrary comparator; the weighted arbitrary-comparator version and q=0 finite-product recurrence extend the minimizer/positive-A source calculation.
mathematical_review.counterexample: For f(t)=t^2/2, alpha=1/2,beta=1,h=-1,x=0,z=1, source (3.3) energy left side is 2 and right side is 3/2. For descent at x=1, f(2)-f(1)=3/2>1/2. Hence the h>=0 boundary cannot be erased.
